exampleCode:
import { createMongoAbility, AbilityBuilder } from '@casl/ability';
import { accessibleBy } from '@casl/mongoose';

// Define permissions once
const { can, cannot, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createMongoAbility);

can('read', ['Post', 'Comment']);
can('manage', 'Post', { author: 'me' });
can('create', 'Comment');

const ability = build();

// Enforce them across your application
ability.can('read', 'Post') // UI & API
accessibleBy(ability, 'update').ofType('Post') // Database conditions

claims.title: Claims
claims.description: Start with feature access or simple capabilities expressed as actions.
claims.example:
import { AbilityBuilder, createMongoAbility } from '@casl/ability';

const { can, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createMongoAbility);

can('read:project');
can('update:project');
can('manage:workspace');

const ability = build();

ability.can('update:project'); // true
claims.detail: A stable API for simple permissions, ready to gain resource context when you need it.

actions.title: Actions / Subjects
actions.description: Give every layer a shared vocabulary: what action, on which resource?
actions.example:
import { AbilityBuilder, createMongoAbility } from '@casl/ability';

const { can, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createMongoAbility);

can('read', 'Project');
can('update', 'Project');
can('manage', 'Workspace');

const ability = build();

ability.can('update', 'Project'); // true
actions.detail: The same capability vocabulary now distinguishes articles, projects, and workspaces.

rbac.title: RBAC
rbac.description: Map roles to rules once, instead of scattering role checks across features.
rbac.example:
import { AbilityBuilder, createMongoAbility } from '@casl/ability';

const { can, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createMongoAbility);
const user = { role: 'projectAdmin' };

can('read', 'Project');
if (user.role === 'projectAdmin') can('update', 'Project');
if (user.role === 'workspaceAdmin') can('manage', 'Workspace');
const ability = build();

ability.can('update', 'Project'); // true
rbac.detail: Roles become bundles of action/resource permissions.

abac.title: ABAC
abac.description: Refine permissions with ownership, tenant identity, or resource state.
abac.example:
import { AbilityBuilder, createMongoAbility, subject } from '@casl/ability';

const { can, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createMongoAbility);
const user = { tenantId: 'tenant-1', role: 'projectAdmin' };

can('read', 'Project', { tenantId: user.tenantId });
if (user.role === 'projectAdmin') {
  can('update', 'Project', { tenantId: user.tenantId });
}
if (user.role === 'workspaceAdmin') {
  can('manage', 'Workspace', { tenantId: user.tenantId });
}

const ability = build();
const project = subject('Project', { ... });
ability.can('update', project); // true
abac.detail:
Roles can still grant permissions; attributes constrain which records those grants cover.

For object checks, subject identifies a plain object as a Project so ability.can applies Project rules to its attributes. See subject type detection.

rebac.title: ReBAC
rebac.description: Add workspace membership and resource administrator relationships on top of tenant isolation.

denormalized.label: Denormalized
denormalized.example:
import { AbilityBuilder, createMongoAbility, subject } from '@casl/ability';

const { can, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createMongoAbility);
const user = { id: 'alice', tenantId: 'tenant-1', role: 'projectAdmin' };

can('update', 'Project', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  projectAdminIds: { $in: [user.id] },
  workspaceMemberIds: { $in: [user.id] }
});

const ability = build();

const project = subject('Project', {
  tenantId: 'tenant-1',
  workspaceMemberIds: ['alice'],
  projectAdminIds: ['alice']
});
ability.can('update', project); // true
denormalized.detail:
Denormalized: Fast, local permission checks. Requires keeping derived membership attributes synchronized.

For object checks, subject identifies a plain object as a Project so CASL checks Project rules against its relationship attributes. See subject type detection.

sql.label: SQL relations
sql.example:
import { AbilityBuilder } from '@casl/ability';
import { createPrismaAbility, accessibleBy } from '@casl/prisma';
import { prismaClient } from './prisma-client.ts';

const { can, build } = new AbilityBuilder(createPrismaAbility);
const user = { id: 'alice', tenantId: 'tenant-1', role: 'projectAdmin' };

can('update', 'Project', {
  tenantId: user.tenantId,
  memberships: {
    some: { userId: user.id, role: 'projectAdmin' }
  }
});

const projects = await prismaClient.project.findMany({
  where: accessibleBy(ability, 'update').ofType('Project')
});
sql.detail: SQL relations: Use @casl/prisma or @ucast/sql for relation filters. Your application loads the referenced relations for object checks; database queries can use the same rules without duplicating membership lists.

evolution.caption: Complementary models, not mandatory migrations. RBAC, ABAC, and relationship-derived permissions can coexist.
